vc-granja-m-viader.why: Cacaolat — Spain's cold cocoa-milk drink, tasted by the Viaders at a wedding during Budapest's 1931 International Fair, then reworked and patented back home in December 1931 (reputedly the world's first industrially made chocolate milk) — is, by the family's account, born of this granja, which five generations have kept pouring thick chocolate and mel i mató rather than reinventing itself. vc-granja-m-viader.person: Joan Viader Roger patented Cacaolat in December 1931; the granja is run today by his descendant Mercè Casademunt Viader and her son Marc — the fourth and fifth generations of the Viader family.

vq-bacoa-kiosko-little-bacoa.why: El Born gourmet-burger pioneer since 2010; stone-grilled patties, small counter, order and queue.
vq-bacoa-kiosko-little-bacoa.address: Av. del Marquès de l'Argentera, 1, El Born / La Ribera, 08003 Barcelona
vq-bacoa-kiosko-little-bacoa.verdict: It is the lead entry in Time Out Barcelona's burger guide and won the magazine's 2010 Best Sandwich award, but the independent 15-seat 2010 pioneer is now flagged closed and the brand survives as an AmRest-owned mini-chain (the operator of Burger King and Pizza Hut Spain).
vq-bacoa-kiosko-little-bacoa.signature: The house Bacoa: stone-grilled patty, smoked bacon, manchego, cheddar, pickles, artisan mustard, smoky char.
vq-bacoa-kiosko-little-bacoa.caveat: A small counter spot with no reservations, so expect a queue. Time Out flags the original "Little Bacoa" (Colomines, 2) as closed; the still-open Born door is the Kiosko on Av. del Marquès de l'Argentera, 1, which is AmRest-run rather than the independent original.

signal_chip.label: Time Out top
signal_chip.full: Time Out Barcelona, 'The best burgers in the city' guide — Bacoa is the lead entry, its three locations opening the list; also Time Out Barcelona 'Best Sandwich' award winner, 2010.
signal_chip.cosign: Time Out credits founder Brad Ainsworth as the man who brought the gourmet burger to Barcelona, stone-grilled for an inimitable smoky flavour.

vc-flash-flash.name: Flash Flash
tags: Open since 1970: fifty-plus tortillas under the black-and-white 'Flash Flash girl' murals.
vc-flash-flash.why: The cult object is the room itself: Federico Correa and Alfonso Mila's white leather banquettes and the life-size black-and-white 'Flash Flash girl' - silhouettes of model Karin Leiz copied from Leopoldo Pomes's photographs - a 1970 design largely intact, beneath which Barcelonans have eaten fifty-plus versions of the Spanish omelette for over half a century. Open since 1970: fifty-plus tortillas under the black-and-white 'Flash Flash girl' murals.
vc-flash-flash.address: Carrer de la Granada del Penedes 25, Sant Gervasi-Galvany, 08006 Barcelona
vc-flash-flash.verdict: You come for the near-intact 1970 room and its Karin Leiz wall images, not for cooking that beats a good neighbourhood bar: the tortillas are competent rather than revelatory and, at roughly EUR 20-30 a head, priced above a corner-bar omelette.
vc-flash-flash.signature: The tortilla de patatas de toda la vida, the plain classic among fifty-plus versions
vc-flash-flash.caveat: Uptown in residential Sant Gervasi-Galvany, off the tourist trail; pricey for what is essentially an omelette (roughly EUR 20-30 a head, under EUR 35 per Guia Repsol); takes no reservations, first-come-first-served, so arrive early. Not a gourmet destination.
vc-flash-flash.person: Leopoldo Pomes (1931-2019), photographer and co-founder, who shot the images of model Karin Leiz behind the black-and-white 'Flash Flash girl' silhouettes that still line the walls; the interior itself was designed by architects Federico Correa and Alfonso Mila.
